input: Start a nature journal with pressed leaves and sketches

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: Knowing whether this is just leaves or also includes other specimens (flowers, feathers, bark rubbings, insects) determines how to set up the journal structure and gathering supplies.
Whether this is for a child, an adult hobbyist, or a student affects the complexity of labeling, the style of sketches, and the tone of written entries.
The specific outdoor environment (backyard, local park, hiking trails, seasonal forest) shapes what materials will be collected and how frequently journal sessions happen.
Budget determines whether to buy a dedicated journal, pressing tools, and art supplies, or to improvise with household materials like heavy books and printer paper.
Whether the journal leans more scientific (species ID, notes, labels) or artistic (decorative layouts, watercolour washes) fundamentally changes what to emphasise in the plan.
Knowing whether 'done well' means completing a first full entry, filling an entire journal, or building a consistent weekly habit changes how milestones and next steps are structured.
Identifying the very first physical action — buying a journal, collecting the first leaf, or setting up a pressing station — determines where to start the step-by-step plan.

gold.taskTitle: Start a nature journal with pressed leaves and sketches
gold.taskDescription: The user wants to create a personal nature journal that combines pressed leaves and hand-drawn sketches as a regular creative or observational practice.

questions.title: What natural materials will you collect beyond leaves?
questions.description: Will the journal include only leaves, or also flowers, seeds, feathers, bark rubbings, or other found specimens?

questions.title: Who is this journal primarily for?
questions.description: Is this for yourself as an adult, a child you are guiding, a class, or a shared family project?

questions.title: Where will you mainly collect your nature specimens?
questions.description: Do you have a backyard, nearby park, woodland trails, or another specific outdoor setting in mind?

questions.title: How much do you want to spend on supplies?
questions.description: Are you looking to use household items only, spend a small amount on basics, or invest in quality art and pressing materials?

questions.title: Should the journal feel more scientific or more artistic?
questions.description: Do you want detailed species labels and field notes, decorative creative layouts, or a blend of both?

questions.title: What does a successfully started journal look like to you?
questions.description: Is success completing one first entry, filling a full journal over time, or establishing a regular weekly journaling habit?

questions.title: Do you already have a journal or any art supplies on hand?
questions.description: Knowing what you already own determines the very first practical step — gathering materials versus heading straight outside to collect.
